dedupe_keys.name: global development potential indices dpis for 13 energy mining and agriculture sectors

description: The development potential indices are global land suitability maps showing where future development of 13 sectors is most likely, accounting for both resource potential and development feasibility. They cover the globe at 1 km resolution for concentrated solar power, photovoltaic solar, wind, hydropower, coal, conventional and unconventional oil and gas, metallic and non-metallic mining, and crop and biofuel expansion, each with a continuous index, a classified index and a classified uncertainty raster, plus parameter descriptions and sensitivity reports. They were produced by J. R. Oakleaf, C. M. Kennedy, S. Baruch-Mordo, J. S. Gerber, P. C. West, J. A. Johnson and J. Kiesecker and described in Scientific Data in June 2019. The figshare collection (version 2, March 2020) makes the per-sector zip files available for free download under CC0, with four further zip files of inputs and Python scripts of about 65 GB. Caveats: reproducing the indices needs ESRI ArcGIS with Advanced and Spatial Analyst licences, and the maps show suitability, not planned projects. They support siting and scenario work for future energy and extractive infrastructure and its land conflicts; a related record is the WorldPop harmonised covariates.
